title: Repair F1: preflight declared operations instead of a future model tool choice
description:
Repair dispatch for PR #543 review finding **F1** (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020
W10). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12` — its notes carry the review
and the integrating agent's verification. This is a MATERIAL, architectural
change to the pre-model discovery/preflight boundary.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.9`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.9`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12` AFTER the F2 repair merged into it. Dependencies
installed. Touch nothing outside it.

Supersedes `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.6`, which recorded this as a deferred finding.
Close that bead as part of this work, pointing at your commit.

## The defect

W10's acceptance requires the DELIVERED text to carry a positive bounded
capability contract, and M10 to compare discovery's preflight against the real
runtime invocation. The live `intervene` path delivers the NEGATIVE form for
P8 and records the real `use_item(hit-target)` invocation in
`m10.runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket`.

Verified root cause, `packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:230`:

```ts
if (leaf.path.endsWith('/operationId') && typeof leaf.value === 'string') {
```

The `capability-preflight` signal fires only when the pre-model state already
contains an `/operationId` leaf. Real campaign state deliberately does not
synthesize one, because **which operation gets invoked is a future model tool
choice**. So pre-model capability selection depends on a parameter that does
not exist until after the model has chosen — the generalized defect, not a P8
quirk.

**Do not fix this by putting an `operationId` into fixture or runtime state.**
The review explicitly forbids it, and it would encode a prediction of the
model's choice as though it were campaign state.

## The decided approach

Capability **availability** is a property of the record plus the item's own
state. It is not a prediction of which operation the model will pick. So
discovery stops waiting to be told an operation and instead enumerates the
operations the record itself declares, preflighting each.

Verified against the real pack:

| record | declared operations |
|---|---|
| `magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3` | `hit-target` (1) |
| `magic-item:cube-of-force` | `press-face-1`…`press-face-6`, `spell-contact-loss` (7) |
| `magic-item:ring-of-protection` | none |

That distribution is the point: P8 gets a real positive contract, the cube is a
genuine multi-operation case, and the ring keeps an honest "no capability
positively selected".

**`variantId` stays an input and is NOT enumerated.** It is a property of the
item instance in inventory, so it is genuinely available pre-model, and
`deriveItemOperationReadinessInput(record, variantId, operationId)` resolves
the operation set through `effectiveMagicItemMechanics(record, variantId)` —
the operation set is variant-dependent. Enumerate operations *for the
instance's actual variant*. Enumerating variants too would preflight item
states the campaign is not in.

**Enumerate the union** of `mechanics.operations[].id` and the non-null
`mechanics.stateMachine.transitions[].via` ids.
`deriveItemOperationReadinessInput` accepts `activate`/`deactivate` sourced
from a state-machine transition even when `operations` does not list them
(read that function before you write the enumeration), so an
`operations`-only walk would under-enumerate a record whose activation lives
only in its state machine. For the cube the two sets coincide; do not conclude
from that that one of them is redundant.

## What to change

1. **`signals.ts`** — the `capability-preflight` signal derives from the BOUND
   ITEM INSTANCE, not from an `/operationId` leaf: for each item instance the
   scenario binds (and each state-referenced item record), emit a preflight
   signal per declared operation, carrying `operationId` and the instance's
   `variantId` as evidence. An explicit `/operationId` in state, where one
   exists, must not produce a duplicate preflight for the same
   `(record, variant, operation)` triple.
2. **`packet.ts`** — `capability()` returns the preflight for ONE
   `(record, variant, operation)` triple today. A candidate can now carry
   several, so `PacketCandidate.capability?: CapabilityPreflight` becomes a
   list. Name it so the plural reads as the bounded set it is, and keep the
   existing `available` / `blocked` derivation per entry unchanged — this
   change is about WHICH triples get preflighted, not about how a preflight is
   judged.
3. **`packetMessage.ts`** — render every contract in the candidate's block.
   The negative form ("no capability was positively selected", with its full
   disclaimer) now applies when the bounded set is EMPTY. A record that
   declares operations but whose every preflight is `blocked` is not the
   negative case: it is a set of blocked contracts, and each still states that
   a blocked contract is not an executable capability.
4. **`measurements.ts` M10** — already pairs on the
   `(recordKey, operationId, variantId)` subject, so it should extend
   naturally to a set. Verify that `runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket` empties
   for P8 and that a runtime invocation of an operation the packet did NOT
   preflight is still reported there.
5. **`shadow.ts`'s `assertV2`** — follow the packet shape change so the durable
   reader admits the bounded set and still fails closed on a malformed entry.

## Evidence required

The reviewer named this evidence specifically; it is the acceptance bar.

E1. A real P8 `intervene` turn where the ACTUAL DM input contains the positive
    bounded contract for `hit-target` — operation, capability id, revision,
    inputs, exclusions, residual interpretation — asserted against the model's
    captured `ModelCompleteInput`, not against the offline packet.
E2. The same turn's M10 contains a REAL discovery/runtime comparison that
    reports `agreed`, and `m10.runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket` is empty.
E3. The adversarial non-fixture-specific case: a different operation and a
    different variant. Use `magic-item:cube-of-force`'s multi-operation set,
    and the variant-bearing item in
    `packages/core/test/discovery/support/variantReadinessAddon.ts`. Prove the
    packet preflights the operations the record declares for the instance's
    actual variant, that a runtime invocation of one of them pairs and agrees,
    and that an invocation of an operation the record does NOT declare is
    reported as absent from the packet rather than silently paired.
E4. `magic-item:ring-of-protection` (P11) declares no operations: the delivered
    text carries the negative form with its full disclaimer and no contract.
E5. The blocked case stays distinct from the negative case — a blocked contract
    is rendered as a contract, not as "no capability positively selected".
E6. The offline probe suites still report their pinned M1–M9, and the
    intervention suite's pinned per-probe report is updated deliberately:
    name every pinned number that moved and why in your notes. Numbers WILL
    move — P7 and P8 gain capability entries — and a pin that silently
    absorbed the change would defeat the pin.

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape an existing test to make this pass. Tests
  that encode the old operationId-driven selection SHOULD change — name each
  and why.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, or the
  design document.
- House style: read the doc comments in `discovery/types.ts`, `packet.ts` and
  `shadow.ts` and match them. Every non-obvious shape says WHY it has that form
  and what wrong thing it makes unrepresentable.
- Known flake: `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs`
  times out at 10s under full-suite load. Pre-existing, filed, unrelated.
  Confirm standalone, note it, do not fix it.
notes:
F1 repair complete at commit 9d37624 on branch eshyra-o9bd.19.12.9 (parent b181e2f).

PRODUCTION CHANGE
- packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts: new exported declaredItemOperationIds(record, variantId) -- union of mechanics.operations[].id and non-null mechanics.stateMachine.transitions[].via, reusing validateRecordReferences (same validation deriveItemOperationReadinessInput runs). Exported from internal.ts.
- packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts: capability-preflight signals now derive from (a) each item INSTANCE the scenario binds (scenario.itemInstances matched via a state leaf) carrying its own variantId, and (b) each record named directly in state via a literal key leaf (KEY_RE match), using a scenario-global variantId fallback. Deduped per (recordKey,variantId) via a Map keyed "recordKey::variantId". One signal emitted per enumerated operationId. The old /operationId-leaf special case is gone entirely; a record reached only by name-mention gets nothing. operationIdsFor() catches ItemStateError (incl. wrapped MagicItemVariantError) and returns [] rather than aborting discovery.
- packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts: PacketCandidate.capability?: CapabilityPreflight -> capabilities: readonly CapabilityPreflight[] (always present, empty = negative case).
- packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts: capability() -> preflightOperation() (per-triple) + capabilities() (maps every capability-preflight route on the candidate through preflightOperation; falls back to the pre-existing offline-declaration mechanism, unchanged, when the candidate carries no such route).
- packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts: renders every entry in capabilities; negative form now triggers when the set is empty OR holds only not-evaluated-offline entries (NOT when it holds only blocked entries -- a blocked contract is rendered as a contract, per E5).
- packages/core/src/discovery/measurements.ts: M10 comparisons now trace.packet.candidates.flatMap(item => item.capabilities.map(...)) -- one comparison per preflight entry, same pairing/agreement logic per entry.
- packages/core/src/discovery/shadow.ts: v2 admission (checkTrace) now does each(item_.capabilities, ..., checkCapability) (array, required) instead of optional(item_.capability, ...) -- fails closed on the old singular shape.

TEST COUNTS
Baseline (b181e2f): 5341 passed / 20 skipped (core+cli combined, per dispatch).
After repair: 5343 passed / 20 skipped. npm run check clean, npm run typecheck clean, npm run verify:worktree green end to end (format fixed 5 files, no semantic changes beyond mine). Known flake packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > "packs publishable tarballs" confirmed passing standalone; not touched.
Net +2 tests: +1 shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts (new E3 adversarial case), +1 packetIntervention.test.ts (new P7 offline multi-op case). discoveryStages.test.ts, shadowRuntime.test.ts, shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts, campaignRuleConsumption.test.ts: net 0 (existing tests rewritten/renamed in place; one speculative test I drafted and then deleted in shadowRuntime.test.ts before running anything, so it never shipped).

PER-RECORD OPERATION SETS ACTUALLY ENUMERATED (verified against the real dnd5e-srd-5.1 pack; matches the bead's table exactly)
- magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3: ['hit-target'] (1 op; mechanics.operations only, no stateMachine)
- magic-item:cube-of-force: ['press-face-1'..'press-face-6','spell-contact-loss'] (7 ops; mechanics.operations and stateMachine.transitions[].via sets coincide exactly, confirmed via a real pack scan -- did not treat that coincidence as license to enumerate only one side); every one of the 7 preflights to 'blocked' (every operation's readiness clause is engine-pending)
- magic-item:ring-of-protection: [] (0 ops, no stateMachine -> negative form, E4)
- magic-item:gem-of-brightness (shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts's pre-existing fixture, not in the diagnostic corpus): ['shed-light','blinding-beam','blinding-cone','end-light'] (4 ops; all blocked, confirmed via readiness-clause scan)
- magic-item:test-variant-readiness (variantReadinessAddon.ts, synthetic): ['spend-one-use'] (1 op; readiness genuinely differs by variant -- available for READY_VARIANT_ID, blocked for PENDING_VARIANT_ID)

PINNED NUMBERS THAT MOVED, AND WHY
1. packetIntervention.test.ts, P8/default, main per-probe loop: M10 flipped from `comparisons: []` + `runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket` holding the hit-target invocation, TO `comparisons` holding one agreed entry + `runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket: []`. Why: the character's ammunition is a real inventory row (installProbeCampaignState) before the model runs, so the held INSTANCE now gets its declared hit-target operation preflighted; the pre-repair code required a literal /operationId leaf that real campaign state never carries and therefore never fired at runtime.
2. packetIntervention.test.ts, same fixture: the delivered message flipped from "no capability was positively selected" to a real "POSITIVE BOUNDED CONTRACT ... status=available" block, for the same reason.
3. PINNED_M9_MEASURED and PINNED_E5_CHECKED in packetIntervention.test.ts did NOT move -- verified: no fixture's requiredRetainedFacts references a capability field, so retained-fact counts are untouched by this repair. Recording this explicitly per E6's instruction that an unchanged pin should be reported as checked, not silently assumed.
4. discoveryStages.test.ts: cube-of-force's capability count moved 1 -> 7 (all blocked) in the rewritten "enumerates every declared operation..." test; ammunition's stayed at 1 (only op it has).
5. shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts "pairing and identity" suite: GEM's capability count moved (effectively) 1 -> 4. comparisons[0] no longer names the operation under test (BLOCKED_OPERATION='blinding-beam' is NOT first in declaration order -- shed-light is), so measured() now returns {m10, comparison} where comparison is picked by the SAME index BLOCKED_OPERATION holds in the candidate's own capabilities array, rather than assuming index 0.
6. shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts VALID fixture: cube-of-force's capability count moved 1 -> 7 (all blocked); the "rejects an evaluated capability missing X" admission tests now break capabilities[0].<key> (path capabilities[0].<key> in the rejection message) instead of capability.<key>.
7. shadowRuntime.test.ts "capability events survive an audit-rejected attempt > keeps the rejected attempt's invocation after its writes roll back": M10 flipped from comparisons:[] / absent-from-packet:[attempt 1] to one agreed comparison / absent-from-packet:[] -- same root cause as #1 (ammo-1 is a real inventory row).

EVERY EXISTING TEST I CHANGED, AND WHY
- itemState.ts: no existing tests changed (only new export added).
- signals.ts / packet.ts / packetMessage.ts / measurements.ts / shadow.ts: production only, no tests live there.
- discoveryStages.test.ts:
  - "quotes the W13 capability contract instead of restating it": mechanical .capability -> .capabilities[0]/find, no behavior change (ammunition has exactly 1 op).
  - "reports a blocked preflight for an engine-pending operation" -> renamed "enumerates every declared operation and reports each engine-pending one as blocked": rewritten to assert the full 7-operation set, all blocked, instead of the one operation an /operationId leaf used to name. Encoded the old single-operation-selection model; changed because that model is exactly what F1 removes.
  - "preflights only the candidate the capability route selected" -> renamed "preflights a state-referenced item but not one reached only by name-mention": the OLD test's premise ("only the item bearing the literal chosen operationId gets a capability") is the defect itself -- it asserted that a SECOND state-referenced magic item (reached via a different field name, not name-mention) got NO capability, which is now wrong by design (every state-referenced item is preflighted). Rewritten to test the real boundary the repair preserves: state-reference vs. mere name-mention. Also had to loosen an assertion mid-implementation: the real pack declares a typed-relationship route between ammunition and cube-of-force I hadn't anticipated, so the name-mentioned candidate's route list is checked with arrayContaining + not.toContain('capability-preflight') rather than an exact array.
  - "reports the readiness capability itself, not an execution capability" and "gates the preflight on the selected variant": mechanical .capability -> .capabilities[0]/find renames; dropped the now-decorative operationId field from stateFields in the variant test since it no longer selects anything.
- shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts: captureForOperation's doc comment updated (no longer "preflights one specific operation"); packetCapability(trace) -> packetCapability(trace, operationId) (finds the specific entry); the "compares a blocked runtime event..." test now uses arrayContaining over comparisons instead of a single-element exact array, because GEM's candidate now carries 4 entries; the entire "pairing and identity" describe block's measured() helper now returns {m10, comparison} picked by index rather than m10 alone with an assumed comparisons[0], for the same reason (see pinned-number item 5); the "refuses to compare a packet status that evaluated nothing" test now maps every entry in candidate.capabilities to not-evaluated-offline instead of rewriting a single optional field.
- shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts: "holds the rich state the cases below rely on" now asserts capabilities.length > 1 and every entry blocked, instead of a single capability object; the two "rejects an evaluated capability missing X" admission tests target capabilities.0.<key> / expect the message to contain capabilities[0].<key>.
- campaignRuleConsumption.test.ts: both tests using CUBE_SCENARIO (cube declares no operationId-specific route anymore, so all 7 preflight) now do packetCandidate(trace, CUBE)?.capabilities.find(item => item.operationId === 'press-face-1') instead of reading .capability directly.
- shadowRuntime.test.ts: "records a runtime capability outcome the shadow packet never preflighted" renamed to "pairs a runtime capability invocation with the preflight the held item declares", with its whole premise inverted (see pinned-number item 7); I initially added a companion test asserting the OLD "absent from packet" behavior still holds when nothing binds the item in state, using a phantom instanceId -- deleted it before it was ever committed once I traced useItem() and confirmed an undeclared/unbound instanceId throws ItemStateError BEFORE the capability-preflight boundary runs, so no RuntimeCapabilityInvocation event is ever recorded for that case; there is nothing real to assert as "absent."
- support/factEvidence.ts: 'cube-blocked-by-readiness' assertion now finds the press-face-1 entry in capabilities instead of reading .capability directly.
- packetIntervention.test.ts: E8-positive-half comment rewritten (no longer describes a real boundary, since the real turn now also reaches the positive contract); the P8-specific block inside the main per-fixture loop flipped from asserting the negative form + absent-from-packet to asserting the positive form + agreed M10 comparison (pinned-number items 1-2); added one new test proving P7's offline packet states a contract for all 7 cube-of-force operations, all blocked (satisfies E3's "P7 gains a capability entry" for this file specifically, since P7's REAL turn never state-references cube-of-force -- it is reached only by name-mention at runtime, so P7's per-probe report in the main loop is otherwise unchanged; recorded as a concern below).

E3 (ADVERSARIAL CASE) EVIDENCE
Added to shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts: uses magic-item:test-variant-readiness (variantReadinessAddon.ts) bound as a real inventory row with a specific variant, proves (a) the packet preflights exactly the one operation the record declares for the INSTANCE'S ACTUAL variant (never the other variant), (b) a real use_item invocation through the tool registry pairs with it in agreement, and (c) an invocation naming an operation the record does not declare is reported absent from the packet rather than paired. (c) is necessarily a hand-built RuntimeCapabilityInvocation, not a live useItem() call -- see "could not do" below.

COULD NOT DO / LIMITATION
Could not produce a REAL runtime invocation of "an operation the record does not declare" to prove the negative-pairing half of E3 (and I removed a shadowRuntime.test.ts test that assumed this was possible). Traced itemState.ts useItem(): deriveItemOperationReadinessInput() throws ItemStateError for an undeclared operationId BEFORE preflightCampaignItemOperation()/onCapabilityInvocation() runs, so no capability event is ever recorded for that call -- there is structurally nothing for M10 to receive. The synthetic event in the new E3 test documents this in a comment and mirrors the existing event() pattern shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts already uses for pairing states that need no execution.

CONCERN ABOUT THE APPROACH / OPEN QUESTION
"P7 and P8 gain capability entries" in the spec is fully true offline (discoveryStages.test.ts, packetIntervention.test.ts's new P7 test, shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts's VALID fixture) but P7's REAL runtime per-probe report in packetIntervention.test.ts's main loop is UNCHANGED: installProbeCampaignState only seeds real inventory for P8; P7's cube-of-force is reached at runtime only by name-mention (never state-referenced), so it never gets a real capability-preflight signal and the main loop's P7 assertions did not need to move. This is the correct, intentional behavior under the repair (name-mention is never grounds for preflight), but it means P7's real-turn behavior is unverified by this suite the way P8's now is. Filed no new bead for this since it is not a defect -- flagging it so the reviewer doesn't expect a P7 real-turn M10 change that legitimately isn't there.

Pre-existing, out of scope, not touched: p08Ammunition.ts's expectedCapabilityStatus.capabilityId is annotated 'magic-item-single-use-spend' but the actual packet capabilityId is 'assertMagicItemOperationReady' (contract.operationId) -- this field is descriptive-only (fixtureContract.ts shape-validates it but nothing cross-checks it against the real packet), predates this bead, and packet.ts's own doc comment already explains why 'magic-item-single-use-spend' was rejected as a name. Not fixed here; noting it in case a future bead wants the fixture annotation corrected to match.
